title: Lagrange, Cauchy, and Sylow existence
section: Part B: Abstract Algebra ▷ Some Theorems Concerning Subgroups
terms: Lagrange theorem; Cauchy theorem; Sylow first theorem; Sylow subgroup; subgroup order; index of a subgroup.

exposition.text:
Lagrange’s theorem states that |H| divides |G| for a subgroup H of a finite group G; the quo-
tient [G : H] = |G|/|H| is its index. Consequently every element order divides |G|, and every
group of prime order is cyclic. The converse fails for arbitrary finite groups: a divisor need not
occur as a subgroup order.
Cauchy’s theorem guarantees an element, hence subgroup, of order p for each prime p | |G|. If
k
p is the largest power of p dividing |G|, Sylow’s first theorem guarantees a subgroup of order
k j
p ; subgroups of order p exist for every 0 ≤ j ≤ k. Finite Abelian groups have subgroups of
every divisor order. Finite cyclic groups have exactly one subgroup of each divisor order, and
every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic.
The alternating group A has order twelve but no subgroup of order six, a standard failure of
4
the converse of Lagrange. In an Abelian group, subgroups exist for every divisor order, but they
need not be cyclic. Cauchy plus commutativity does guarantee a cyclic subgroup whose order
is the product of any selected distinct prime divisors, by multiplying elements of those coprime
orders.

question.text:
A group has order 180. Which order is guaranteed for one of its subgroups by Sylow existence?
(A) 10 (B) 12 (C) 15 (D) 20 (E) 9

solution.text:
2 2
Since 180 = 2 · 3 · 5, Sylow existence guarantees subgroups of orders 4, 9, and 5, and their
prime-power subgroups. Among these choices only 9 is such a guaranteed prime power.
The question specifies what follows from Sylow existence alone.

question.text:
How many subgroups does a cyclic group of order 360 have?
(A) 12 (B) 18 (C) 24 (D) 30 (E) 36

solution.text:
3 2
There is exactly one subgroup for every divisor. Since 360 = 2 3 5, the divisor count is (3 +
1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 24.

question.text:
A finite group contains an element of order seven but no element of order three or five. Which
could be its order?
(A) 21 (B) 28 (C) 35 (D) 42 (E) 70

solution.text:
Lagrange requires the group order to be divisible by seven. Cauchy excludes any order di-
visible by three or five, leaving twenty-eight. The cyclic group of order twenty-eight realizes
the conditions, since its element orders divide twenty-eight.

question.text:
How many subgroups of order six does A , the group of even permutations of four symbols,
4
have?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 4

solution.text:
Such a subgroup would have index two and hence be normal, giving a quotient of order
two. Every three-cycle must map to the quotient identity, because its image has order
dividing both three and two. There are eight three-cycles, so the subgroup would contain
them and the identity, more than six elements. This contradicts its proposed size and
disproves the general converse to Lagrange.

question.text:
Every Abelian group of order 72 must contain a cyclic subgroup of which order?
(A) 4 (B) 6 (C) 8 (D) 9 (E) 12

solution.text:
Cauchy gives elements of orders two and three. They commute, so their product has order

six, producing the required cyclic subgroup. The group Z × Z has order seventy-two

and every element has order dividing six, ruling out the other guarantees. Existence of a
subgroup of a divisor order does not imply existence of a cyclic subgroup of that order.
